nodes.description: Three of the Seckel genes act on the replication fork itself rather than on the ATR checkpoint that reads it or on the centrosome that divides the cell. TRAIP is an E3 ubiquitin ligase recruited to damage during S phase, NSMCE2 is the SUMO ligase of the SMC5/6 complex, and DNA2 is a replication-associated nuclease-helicase. In each, patient or knockdown cells tolerate replicative stress poorly, and the resulting limit on developmental cell proliferation is the proposed route to the growth and brain-size phenotype. The node is kept separate from the ATR node because each of the three reports describes its gene acting at the fork itself rather than through ATR checkpoint signalling; that is a statement about what those reports show, not a claim that no such link exists.
